question: What level of contact does primary health care represent within a national health system?

options.B: The tertiary level of specialized care

explanation: Primary health care is designed to be the initial entry point where individuals and communities interact with the health system. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is primary health care considered essential for resource-constrained health systems?

options.A: It restricts health access exclusively to urban populations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for specialized surgical interventions
options.C: It prevents tertiary hospitals from becoming overwhelmed by minor conditions
options.D: It relies entirely on high-cost imported medical technologies

explanation: Managing routine health needs at the community level ensures that major hospitals can focus on complex, specialized cases. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h1)

question: What model dominated global health care delivery prior to the Alma-Ata conference?

options.D: A hospital-centric and curative medical model

explanation: Before 1978, health systems focused heavily on treating established diseases within expensive urban facilities rather than community prevention. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h2)

question: The pre-Alma-Ata medical approach directly contributed to which major problem in rural populations?

options.A: Rapid eradication of vaccine-preventable childhood infections
options.B: Overcrowding of primary health clinics with minor ailments
options.C: Excessive reliance on community health extension workers
options.D: Profound health disparities and a lack of basic care access

explanation: Focusing resources on urban curative centers left rural and marginalized communities with virtually no access to basic health services. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h2)

question: In what year was the historic International Conference on Primary Health Care held at Alma-Ata?
explanation: The landmark Alma-Ata declaration shaping modern primary health care took place in September 1978. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT an essential component outlined by the Alma-Ata declaration?

options.B: Maternal and child health care including family planning

explanation: The Alma-Ata declaration focused on foundational, accessible community care rather than high-technology specialized hospital procedures. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h3)

question: What agency was established in Nigeria in 1992 to spearhead grassroots health delivery?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Specialized Tertiary Hospitals
options.B: Nigerian Medical and Dental Regulatory Board
options.C: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

explanation: The National Primary Health Care Development Agency was created to coordinate and drive primary health care implementation across Nigerian communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h4)

question: A persistent challenge affecting primary health care delivery in many rural Nigerian centers is:

options.A: Infrastructural decay and shortages of health personnel
options.B: The complete absence of common infectious diseases
options.C: An overwhelming surplus of highly specialized surgeons
options.D: Excessive funding that exceeds community absorptive capacity

explanation: Despite strong policy blueprints, Nigerian primary care often struggles with underfunding, poor facilities, and staffing deficits. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h4)

question: What shift in strategy occurred in global health during the late 1980s due to funding constraints?

options.A: A complete abandonment of community-based health interventions
options.B: Selective primary health care focusing on specific high-burden conditions
options.C: The total elimination of all vaccination programs worldwide
options.D: Exclusive investment in luxury private hospital construction

explanation: Critics and policymakers promoted selective primary care to target specific measurable diseases when comprehensive funding fell short. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: How did the Sustainable Development Goals build upon previous global health initiatives?

options.A: By replacing community nurses entirely with automated machines
options.B: By reaffirming universal health coverage as an indispensable target
options.C: By shifting total focus back to expensive urban curative surgery
options.D: By removing all maternal health targets from international policy

explanation: The Sustainable Development Goals renewed the global commitment to achieving universal health coverage and addressing health determinants. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which declaration was adopted in 2018 to revitalize the commitment to primary health care?
explanation: The Astana Declaration was signed in 2018 to renew global dedication to primary health care four decades after Alma-Ata. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h6)

question: A major emphasis of the Astana Declaration regarding health system strengthening is:

options.A: Dismantling community health nursing in favor of mobile apps
options.B: Focusing solely on advanced pharmacological research laboratories
options.C: Restricting health care management exclusively to national governments
options.D: Empowering individuals and communities alongside political commitment

explanation: Astana stresses that sustainable health requires active community empowerment and strong political choices across all societal sectors. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h6)

question: What broad category of diseases is increasingly managed by primary care nurses alongside traditional infectious conditions?

options.B: Rare genetic disorders requiring bone marrow transplantation
options.C: Non-communicable diseases such as hypertension and diabetes
options.D: Acute traumatic injuries requiring intensive neurosurgery

explanation: Modern primary care nurses frequently manage chronic non-communicable conditions within community health centers. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)

question: A primary care nurse in a rural Nigerian clinic notices an increasing prevalence of uncontrolled hypertension among older adults. Based on primary health care principles, what is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Establish a community-based screening and health education program
options.B: Refer every single adult in the community immediately to a tertiary teaching hospital
options.C: Advise patients to stop seeking healthcare outside their homes
options.D: Wait for international agencies to build a specialized cardiac center

explanation: Primary health care emphasizes early detection, health education, and accessible management at the community level before conditions require tertiary care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h7)
